senses.gloss: f. (v. שְׁמוּעָה) report, tradition, traditional law; outcome of a discussion, decision.
units: <cite ref="Targum of I Chronicles 11:11">Targ. I Chr. XI, 11</cite> (ed. Rahmer <he>שמעת</he>, corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Eruvin 9b">Erub. 9ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Kiddushin 50b">Kidd. 50ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>ומותבינן אשְׁמַעְתִּין</he> but we must bring evidence against the tradition which we just cited; <cite ref="Berakhot 33a:29">Ber. 33ᵃ</cite> <he>אשמעתיה</he> (corr. acc., v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 70).
<cite ref="Sotah 21a:13">Sot. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>דסלקא ליה ש׳ וכ׳</he> a scholar whose final conclusions agree with the adopted practice.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 38b:22">Snh. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>ר״מ</he> … <he>תילתא ש׳ וכ׳</he> R. Meir used to divide his lectures into three parts, one part devoted to legal discussion, one to homily (v. <cite ref="A00247"><he>אֲגָדָה</he></cite>), and one to parables.

<cite ref="Berakhot 6b:13">Ber. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>אגרא דש׳ סברא</he> the merit of studying traditions lies in the reasoning thereon; a. v. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="U01520"><he>שְׁמָעָתָא</he></cite>, <cite ref="U01520"><he>שְׁמַעְתָּתָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Eruvin 65a:13">Erub. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>מחדדן שְׁמָעָתָךְ</he> thou hast thy traditions always ready.
<cite ref="Berakhot 42a:7">Ber. 42ᵃ</cite> <he>לית הילכתא ככל הני ש׳ וכ׳</he> the adopted practice is not in agreement with all these traditions &c.; a. fr.
